whatItIs.text: A rich, opaque liquid pressed from the grated pulp of mature coconuts; thinner and thicker pressings give coconut milk and coconut cream.

historyNote.text: Coconut milk is a traditional ingredient across Southeast Asia, Oceania, South Asia, and East Africa, and spread to the Caribbean, Central America, and West Africa with colonial-era coconut plantings.

howToChoose.text: For cooking, choose full-fat cans without added thickeners where possible; check for dents or bulging and shake lightly (a sloshy can is fine, a solid one may be separated cream).

storage.text: Move leftover canned milk to a covered container in the fridge; it firms up when chilled. The rulebook has the window.
storage.note: opened-can window lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Stir leftover coconut milk into curries, porridge, or rice for richness, or whip the separated cream for desserts.

substitutions.note: for richness in curries; dairy-based and less coconutty, add a squeeze of lime
